scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: The dance serves as a social gathering practice and an avenue for personal improvisation and self-expression within Creole culture.
Today it is a living tradition.
on_screen: Footage: Bear in the Big Blue House LIVE! ON TOUR: The Crossover V2 (https://archive.org/details/bear-in-the-big-blue-house-live-on-tour-the-crossover-v2_202501)

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: Zydeco is danced as a partner dance where the follower usually mirrors the leader's steps, though figures allow for self-expression and improvisation.
Dancers execute small sidewise steps with a relatively steady upper body, keeping the physical feel directed downward into the floor without hip wiggling, swinging, or jumping.
The eight-beat basic cycle is organized as two mirrored four-beat sections ('SPSS SPSS', meaning step-pause-step-step, or slow-quick-quick).
Watch for SPSS Basic Step, Eat-a-Beat, Pulse / Butt Drop.
on_screen: Hero video full screen, 30–45 s (mgv8tQ-15MA)
Captions name each signature move as it appears
Formation: Partner dance in open or closed frame, shuffling in place or rotating together, usually clockwise

scenes.title: Listen
narration: The pulse is 4/4.

Zydeco music is defined by rapid, lively syncopation that drives continuous footwork. The rhythm delivers a pronounced accent on the second and sixth beats of an eight-beat phrase, pulling dancers down into the beat rather than lifting them upward.

scenes.title: Step A — slowly
narration: Step 1: Step onto the left foot on count 1 and hold weight through count 2 (slow)
Step 2: Shift weight onto the right foot on count 3 (quick)
Footwork from the sources: Small sidewise steps, in-place shuffles, and weight shifts structured on an 8-beat rhythm (slow on 1-2, quick on 3, quick on 4; slow on 5-6, quick on 7, quick on 8)
Drill: Count out loud 'slow, quick, quick' (1-2, 3, 4 and 5-6, 7, 8) while transferring weight from left to right
on_screen: Instructor front view, then back view (student's perspective); three repetitions
Counts on screen

scenes.title: Step B — the next layer
narration: Step 3: Shift weight back onto the left foot on count 4 (quick)
Step 4: Step onto the right foot on count 5 and hold weight through count 6 (slow)
Drill: Practice the SPSS step-pause-step-step sequence solo without upper body sway
on_screen: Instructor front and back view; slow, then half tempo

scenes.title: Put it together
narration: Step A, then Step B, without stopping. Slow first.
Now half tempo. Now full tempo.
Mirror: the instructor faces you and mirrors, so your right is your right.
Drill: Maintain a steady, grounded stance with slightly flexed knees
on_screen: Split screen: front view / back view
Tempo label changes: slow → half → full

scenes.title: Common mistakes and what to avoid
narration: Avoid vertical bouncing, jumping, excessive upper-body movement, and hip swinging or wiggling
Teachers of this dance warn against: hoping instead of shifting weight
Teachers of this dance warn against: leading step size from the follower instead of the leader
on_screen: Side-by-side: source-supported correction

Options card: Seated or supported option: Perform weight transfers by tapping alternating feet on the floor: left foot taps and holds on counts 1-2, right foot taps on 3, left foot taps on 4, repeating with right foot lead on counts 5-8. · For children: 'Catch the Beat': Children dance the slow-quick-quick pattern and freeze on counts 2 and 6, or shout 'Eat a Beat!' while kicking or tapping their free foot.
